title: Protocol to visualize distinct motoneuron pools in adult zebrafish via injection of retrograde tracers
protocol: Prepare the injection pin.
Place crystals of the fluorescent dextran dye on a clean glass slide.
Add 2 μL of distilled water to the dye and mix well.
Let the mixture dry for several minutes until it has the consistency of a paste.
Dip the tungsten pin into the dye mixture.
Prepare the fish by placing it in anesthetic solution.
Maintain the fish in the anesthetic solution for about 30–60 seconds until deep anesthesia is reached.
Place the anesthetized fish laterally on a wet paper tissue under a stereo microscope.
Secure the fish position by covering its head and tail with additional paper tissues.
Dry the surface of the zebrafish and scrape away a few scales using forceps to gain better access to the targeted muscle.
Inject the dye-soaked pin into the target muscle fibers.
Soak the pins in the dye multiple times if needed, and repeat the injection.
Let the fish recover from anesthesia in fresh fish tank water.
Keep the animal in a regular fish tank for at least 2 hours or overnight (14–20 hours) to allow for retrograde transport of the tracer.
Deeply anesthetize all the injected fish with 0.1% MS-222 solution.
Place the fish on a paper towel for a few seconds to remove excess water.
Glue the fish laterally on a glass Petri dish using superglue.
Cover the head and tail of the fish with glue and immediately submerge it in 1× PBS.
Remove internal organs, skin first, then muscles to expose vertebrae.
Discard 1× PBS and add 4% PFA in the dish; keep at 4°C for 2–24 hours for optimal fixation.
Discard 4% PFA and rinse once with 1× PBS.
Fill the dish with 1× PBS.
Isolate spinal cord using forceps under a stereomicroscope.
Remove the neural spines and vertebrae arches to facilitate dissection.
Remove the hemal spines and centrum to expose the spinal cord.
Transfer the spinal cord to a multiwell plate filled with 1× PBS.
Store the spinal cord at 4°C until further processing.
Wash the tissue extensively with 1× PBS.
Block non-specific binding sites with blocking solution for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Incubate in primary antibody mix at 4°C for the appropriate amount of time.
Wash extensively with 1× PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibody mix at 4°C overnight.
Cut parafilm to fit the microscope glass slide and cut out the middle where the spinal cord will be placed.
Warm up the parafilm gently on a heating plate to avoid detachment from the glass.
Position the spinal cord in the desired orientation on the slide using forceps.
Add non-hardening mounting media.
Coverslip the sample.
Prepare the Zeiss LSM980-Airy2 confocal microscope equipped with a 20× (NA 1.1) objective.
Focus on the spinal cord using the fluorescence or the bright field.
Move to the acquisition mode and set up the desired channels.
Acquire the part of the spinal cord where MNs were back labeled.
